newsitem.title: GERMANY: German debt comfortably higher, ready to push on.
newsitem.headline: German debt comfortably higher, ready to push on.

text.p: German debt prices spent a somewhat uninspired day sitting comfortably in firm ground, gathering pace for another leg up before the end of the week.

Analysts said the market, although trading sideways for most of Wednesday's session, had got over the hurdle of new cash paper supply in the past two sessions and the June DTB future now looked ready to break higher.
"Given the gains we had yesterday and today, the technical picture is fairly constructive," said Charles Diebel, senior fixed income analyst at Technical Data in London.
June futures were up 13 basis poinst at 100.79 by 1434 GMT.
"Unless we break back down through 100.60, we should be able to retest the 101.13 high by the weekend," said Diebel.
The auction of a second tranche of 10-year government paper due August 2007 went reasonably well, analysts said, although some players had hoped for a better result.
The Bundesbank said earlier that it had sold a further 5.5 billion marks of the new issue at a yield of 5.87 percent. On Tuesday the central bank sold 5.0 billion marks at a 5.80 percent yield.
"The demand was a bit low today, probably because prices were about half a point up on yesterday," said Diebel.
"Some people were looking for a pick-up of around 6.00 billion and so it was a little disappointing."
Latest quotes for the new issue gave a price of 100.81 by 1449 GMT, offering a 5.886 percent yield.
Meanwhile, the old 10-year benchmark Bund due January 2007 was trading at 101.08 in late business for a yield of 5.841 percent.

A report from the European Commission suggesting that all 15 EU states except Italy and Greece were on track to meet the Maastricht criteria for the single European currency failed to excite the Bund market, analysts said.
"They said just about what we expected them to say," said one London based trader. "The market didn't seem to care."
On yield spreads, the 10-year Bund/T-note gap was steady at 113 basis points in late European trade, while spreads to other European debt had narrowed slightly after the upbeat EC forecasts.
